Package com.eqixiac.equinix.design.value.ratecard

package com.eqixiac.equinix.design.value.ratecard
Rate cards: pluggable sources of unit prices for the design-time cost, savings, and TCO models. The central abstraction is RateCard, whose lookups (connection, Cloud Router, cloud egress, colocation) return Optional — an empty result means "this card cannot price that item", which is deliberately distinct from a zero price, so callers fall back to another source instead of treating unknown as free.

Cards are composed into a precedence chain with RateCard.layered(...) — the first card that can price an item wins. The conventional ordering is most-trusted first: CustomRateCard (caller-supplied, e.g. negotiated contract rates), then EquinixRateCard (live Fabric Pricing API, term-aware with labelled substitutions), then ReferenceRateCard (bundled, dated indicative figures). RateCard.standardChain(fabric) builds the default live-then-reference chain the value models use when no card is supplied. Every PriceQuote and EgressRate carries its PriceSource provenance and an optional note flagging substitutions and extrapolations.

Two invariants hold across all cards: an unpriceable item yields empty, never a fabricated $0; and quotes in different currencies are never combined — no FX rate is ever invented (PriceQuote.plus throws on a currency mismatch, and the engines route cross-card sums through CurrencyReconciler).
